Okay, so the first week went AMAZING.

Silicon Stampeders dropped 180.

Inkling Strikers finished at 88.3.

Agents had to deal with some injuries (which wasn’t their fault) and some lineup mistakes (which were their fault).

https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!lwGa!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F59824e1f-b89c-4601-976f-9502dd777d56_1888x1056.jpeg

Now that you’re caught up, here are the final scores for the week.

### Neural Endzone vs The Grokfather

__Neural Endzone (anthropic/claude-sonnet-5) barely beat The Grokfather (x-ai/grok-4.6) 127.9 to 125.__

This was the Tight End Game.

Neural Endzone got a monster night from Amon-Ra St. Brown (28.7) and a TE explosion from Dallas Goedert (23.7). Breece Hall (19.8) did the rest. When I personally did my own drafting I skipped on Goedert for Kyle Pitts, and I’m regretting this descision, but I’m sure Neural Endzone is super happy with this choice.

The Grokfather almost stole it even though all their players did okay. Trey McBride (24.5), Steelers Defense (18.0), and Tyler Loop (14.0) were the stars for the week. I was surprised that Saquon Barkley 9.0 and Tee Higgins 8.9 failed to produce more.

Neither team felt the need to adjust their lineup going into the next week, which looks right to me.

### Quantum Shift vs Inkling Strikers

**Quantum Shift (google/gemini-3.8-flash) defeated Inkling Strikers (thinkingmachines/inkling) 120.5 to 88.3**

Quantum Shift’s roster did fine, and got an acceptable amount of points. Having the first round draft pick means you get Jahmyr Gibbs (33.6) who did exactly what a first round overall pick should do, and and Lamar Jackson (25.0) did fine. Overall a boring result.

The interesting part was on Friday, when it realized Brock Bowers was ruled out. It’s backup, Hunter Henry had already played Thursday and was locked on the bench, which meant it had to do something, and the agent actually did something.

    “backup TE Hunter Henry played Thursday night and is locked on the bench, leaving an unfillable starting TE1 slot without an acquisition.”

They dropped Chris Rodriguez for Brenton Strange. Strange scored 10.3. Bowers scored 0. It was the only free-agent add in the entire league in Week 1.

Inkling Strikers kept Kenneth Walker (34.1) on the bench until the last moment. When I ran the agents on Monday, it noticed Kenneth Walker was still on the bench and moved him last moment.

There seemed to be some confusion for this agent. All week the logs said Walker was already RB2. He wasn’t. Monday night they finally moved him into the starting slot.

    “Kenneth Walker is unlocked (isLineupMoveLocked: false) and expected to play Monday Night. He’s eligible for a starter slot. Let me set the lineup.”

    “Andy Reid indicated he will be fine.”

Walker played, and the Chiefs fed him all night. They still lost, because Jalen Coker (33.8), Deebo Samuel (18.0), and Juwan Johnson (14.4) all sat, Kyle Pitts scored 0, and Houston Defense scored -2. This highlights the pain of fantasy football. I too had Kyle Pitts and lost because he scored zero points. I was pretty upset.

### Starlight Diffusion vs Laguna Swell

**Starlight Diffusion (inception/mercury-2.5) beat Laguna Swell (poolside/laguna-s-2.1) 122.7 to 119.7**

This one was almost a tie game. I didn’t really program the ability to handle ties, I thought the effort of developing this in (or prompting it to write it in) wasn’t worth it because how possible was it?! I almost found out.

For a stretch on Monday the score was 119.7–119.7. Denver’s defense finally kicked in 3 points and Starlight Diffusion escaped.

Starlight Diffusion got Jalen Hurts (24.7), Zay Flowers (26.0), and DJ Moore (21.0). A.J. Brown scored 5.6 and then went IR. I also had A.J Brown on my team so I feel the pain here. Then to make things worse, Flowers went down as well.

Tight end play was wonky this week Starlight Diffusion had Harold Fannin (4.1) starting over Isaiah Likely (27.8). You never know who’s going to do better, but if this was reversed, the game wouldn’t have been so close.

Laguna Swell should have won this game. Josh Allen (35.7). Javonte Williams (24.2). Bucky Irving (20.3). CeeDee Lamb (15.4). All contributed well.

The agents don’t always make correct decisions and this is exactly what happened here.

    “FLEX1: Christian Watson (GB) — ON PUP LIST, OUT for Weeks 1-4 — Must bench”

Watson was not on PUP. Watson scored 32.7.

They started Davante Adams (5.6) and Luther Burden (9.5) instead, and also sat Chuba Hubbard (23.7). Colston Loveland scored 0. Josh Jacobs was inactive. They lost by 3. These were all rookie level mistakes. I wonder if next week they will adjust.

### Fourth Down Thunder vs Spark Blitz Brigade

**Fourth Down Thunder (openai/gpt-5.6-terra) beat Spark Blitz Brigade (meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor) 139.8 to 105.9**

Fourth Down Thunder has a great week. and easily won despite keeping Ashton Jeanty (32.7) on the bench. Starting they had Derrick Henry (35.3), Chris Olave (28.2), and Trevor Lawrence (26.1) doing great things for them. Ja’Marr Chase (3.2) was a dud.

OpenAI’s agent refused to panic:

    “Ja’Marr Chase’s 3.2-point result is a one-week outcome and not, by itself, evidence of a flawed process.”

Fair on Chase, but I’d love to see if this week was enough for Fourth Down Thunder to move Jeanty into a starting position.

Spark Blitz Brigade had Jaxon Smith-Njigba (26.2) and a decent RB pair (Chase Brown 18.8, Travis Etienne 14.8), then put Jaylen Waddle (1.2) in FLEX while Dalton Kincaid (18.0) sat. It happens.

### Silicon Stampeders 180.0 vs Mistral Maulers 110.5

**Silicon Stampeders (nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra) racked up SO MANY POINTS to defeat Mistral Maulers (mistralai/mistral-medium-3-5) 180 to 110.5**

The statement game. Caleb Williams 37.3, D’Andre Swift 32.4, Justin Jefferson 31.2, Jonathan Taylor 25.1. These four players outscored some teams’ entire benches. Nvidia’s bench still had Kyle Monangai (20.4)and Parker Washington (19.3). They could have scored 200. Rashee Rice (9.9) was the only starter who looked human. Still the Silicon Stampeders thoughts on Rice:

    “Don’t panic after one slow week from proven talent (Rice) — evaluate target share/snap counts first.”

Still, Mistral Maulers were not bad. Bijan Robinson (31.3) and Nico Collins (21.2) did great. They were just forced to compete against the massive week the Silicon Stampeders had. Some of the bench/not bench decisions are tough. David Montgomery (28.9) and Mike Evans (16.9) sat on the bench for a combined 45 points. They also benched Malik Nabers over injury risk, then put him back in at FLEX on Sunday (12.9) after it seemed he would be fine, and we was, but Montgomery stil managed to g4t more points. Their own recap blamed “over-reliance on draft order.” True enough. Still would not have won.
Interesting details about the week

The league almost tied. Starlight Diffusion vs Laguna Swell sat at 119.7–119.7 until Denver defense. I almost had to write a blog post about how to deal with a tie I didn’t anticipate. Have I learned my lesson? No.

Still some hallucinations. Laguna Swell isn’t being run by a frontier model. Laguna S2.1 made by a company called Poolside is still doing a really good job, but still invented a Watson PUP for Weeks 1–4. I’m wondering if this was just a problem Laguna run into first, or if the more frontier models won’t have this problem.

A team used free agency! Quantum Shift noticed it was going to have a problem with Bowers being out, and needed a solution, so it dropped Strange, added Rodriguez, and it worked out well. This might be might one of the things I’m most excited about. It noticed a problem, figured out a fix, and it worked.

### Week 2 matchups

    Inkling Strikers vs Neural Endzone

    The Grokfather vs Laguna Swell

    Fourth Down Thunder vs Quantum Shift

    Starlight Diffusion vs Silicon Stampeders

    Mistral Maulers vs Spark Blitz Brigade

### Storylines to watch

Does Laguna Swell actually start Christian Watson this time? He’s projected over 11 points, but Chubba Hubbard and George Kittle is on the bench also, so figuring out who to put in that flex spot will be interesting.

Forth Down Thunder HAS to start Ashton Jeanty now right?

Starlight Diffusion has both A.J Brown and Zay Flowers injured. Ideally they will move them out of starting spots, but what do they do with them in general? Hold them? Drop them? We will see.

Can anyone defeat the Silicon Stampeders?!
